citation: Rico-Cabanas L, Martinez-Izquierdo JA (2007) CIRE1, a novel transcriptionally active Ty1-copia retrotransposon from Citrus sinensis. Mol Genet Genomics 277(4):365-377. PMID 17216224. The paper TITLE makes the Ty1-copia assignment; the abstract states CIRE1 is the first complete retrotransposon identified in Citrus, ~2,200 full-length copies, 2.9% of the genome.
why_safe: The Copia call comes from the primary describing paper's own title, and that paper is REFERENCE 1 of the GenBank record itself (verified in the flatfile: Rico-Cabanas & Martinez-Izquierdo, Mol. Genet. Genomics 277(4):365-377 (2007), PUBMED 17216224). No annotation pipeline, no RepeatMasker, no inference from sequence. The deposit IS the element (title is the element, 5,044 bp, no host gene included).

citation: Bhattacharyya MK, Gonzales RA, Kraft M, Buzzell RI (1997) A copia-like retrotransposon Tgmr closely linked to the Rps1-k allele that confers race-specific resistance of soybean to Phytophthora sojae. Plant Mol Biol 34(2):255-264. PMID 9207841. The paper TITLE states 'A copia-like retrotransposon Tgmr'.
why_safe: Label is in the title of the primary paper, which is REFERENCE 1 of the deposit (verified in the flatfile). Deposit is the element only, 'complete sequence'. STRUCTURAL CAVEAT for classifier scoring: the paper reports the element has LTRs and four non-overlapping ORFs but that protease, reverse transcriptase and RNase H are non-functional owing to stop codons - i.e. this is a defective copy. A domain-completeness-based caller may fail it for reasons unrelated to the superfamily label.

citation: White SE, Habera LF, Wessler SR (1994) Retrotransposons in the flanking regions of normal plant genes: a role for copia-like elements in the evolution of gene structure and expression. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 91(25):11792-11796. PMID 7991537. Abstract: the wx-K mutation results from a copia-like retrotransposon insertion into maize waxy exon 12; that element, Hopscotch, 'has one long open reading frame encoding all of the domains required for transposition'.
why_safe: Copia assignment is made in the abstract and title of the primary paper describing this exact element (Hopscotch), and that paper is REFERENCE 2 of the deposit (verified in the flatfile, PUBMED 7991537). The deposit is the element (gag/pol complete cds), not a BAC or contig, and unlike the maize entries already in the corpus it needs no coordinates. Maize is over-represented in the existing corpus but this is a distinct element, distinct accession and distinct paper.

citation: Buti M, Giordani T, Vukich M, Gentzbittel L, Pistelli L, Cattonaro F, Morgante M, Cavallini A, Natali L (2009) HACRE1, a recently inserted copia-like retrotransposon of sunflower (Helianthus annuus L.). Genome 52(11):904-911. PMID 19935914. The paper TITLE states 'copia-like retrotransposon'.
why_safe: The published paper's title carries the Copia assignment for the named element HACRE1, and its abstract describes a complete element with flanking LTRs and an internal region, ~160 copies in the sunflower genome. LINKAGE CAVEAT: the GenBank REFERENCE block still lists the paper as 'Unpublished' (title 'HACRE1, a complete, recently inserted Copia-like retrotransposon of sunflower (Helianthus annuus L.)'), so the accession-to-paper link rests on element name plus submitter identity (Natali L., same senior author) rather than on an accession quoted in the paper - Genome is not open access, so I could not confirm the accession is printed in the article text. The deposit is the element alone, no host gene.

citation: Huang J, Wang Y, Liu W, Shen X, Fan Q, Jian S, Tang T (2017) EARE-1, a transcriptionally active Ty1/Copia-like retrotransposon has colonized the genome of Excoecaria agallocha through horizontal transfer. Front Plant Sci 8:45. PMID 28174588, PMC5258746. Title states Ty1/Copia-like; text describes 'the gag-pol domain order of Ty1/copia-like retroelements: gag, protease (PR), integrase (INT), reverse transcriptase (RT), and RNase H'.
why_safe: Strongest accession-to-paper linkage in this set: the article text itself states the element was 'deposited in GenBank under the accession number KU198316' (verified verbatim from the PMC full text), and the same text gives the Ty1/copia domain order as the basis of the assignment. Length note: 9,555 bp is long for a Ty1/copia element, but the paper independently claims a 'putative full-length (~9550 bp)' element, so the record scope is paper-endorsed rather than a mis-scoped deposit.

citation: Kimura Y, Tosa Y, Shimada S, Sogo R, Kusaba M, Sunaga T, Betsuyaku S, Eto Y, Nakayashiki H, Mayama S (2001) OARE-1, a Ty1-copia retrotransposon in oat activated by abiotic and biotic stresses. Plant Cell Physiol 42(12):1345-1354. PMID 11773527. Title states 'a Ty1-copia retrotransposon in oat'; abstract states 'A complete OARE-1 copy (8,665 bp)' was isolated and classified within the BARE-1 subgroup.
why_safe: Ty1-copia assignment is in the primary paper's title, and the paper also places OARE-1 in the BARE-1 subgroup - BARE-1 is independently an established Copia element (already in this corpus as Z17327), which corroborates the call from a second direction. LINKAGE: the GenBank REFERENCE is 'Unpublished' ('OARE-1, an LTR-retrotransposon isolated from oat'), so the link is inferential, but it is tight - the record length (8,665 bp) matches the paper's stated complete-copy length exactly, and four of the five deposit authors (Kimura, Sogo, Tosa, Nakayashiki, Mayama) are authors on the paper. STRUCTURAL CAVEAT: the DEFINITION calls the gag-pol a pseudogene, so the ORF is disrupted; use for LTR/domain-content, not for intact-ORF testing.

citation: Warren AM, Hughes MA, Crampton JM (1997) Zebedee: a novel copia-Ty1 family of transposable elements in the genome of the medically important mosquito Aedes aegypti. Mol Gen Genet 254(5):505-513. PMID 9197409. Title assigns the family to copia-Ty1; abstract reports phylogenetic placement of 'Zebedee within this group, showing considerable homology to copia from Drosophila melanogaster'.
why_safe: The copia-Ty1 assignment is in the primary paper's title and is supported there by an explicit phylogenetic placement against Drosophila copia; that paper is REFERENCE 1 of the deposit (verified in the flatfile, PUBMED 9197409). Only invertebrate case in this batch and a new order relative to the corpus (Diptera: Culicidae, Aedes). CONFIDENCE MEDIUM, and the reason matters for a panel named ltr-copia: the same abstract states Zebedee elements lack the typical LTR features and gag homologues found in previously characterised copia elements. The superfamily label is published, but this record is a poor exemplar for LTR-boundary or gag-domain testing and should be treated as an atypical member, not a canonical one.

citation: Smyth DR, Kalitsis P, Joseph JL, Sentry JW (1989) Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 86(13):5015-5019, "Plant retrotransposon from Lilium henryi is related to Ty3 of yeast and the gypsy group of Drosophila" (PMID 2544887). Claim supported: the del 1-46 element sequenced in this deposit is Ty3/gypsy. Abstract: pol comparisons show "del to be closely related to the Ty3 retrotransposon of yeast (37-40% identity)" and "del is also related to the gypsy group of Drosophila (17.6, 297, gypsy/mdg4, and 412)".
why_safe: The label comes from the 1989 discovery paper's own amino-acid comparisons of three conserved pol regions against Ty3 and the Drosophila gypsy group, made 15+ years before any modern TE annotation pipeline existed; the paper title states the assignment. The deposit is the element itself (record = del 1-46, 9345 bp, LTRs 1..2406 and the internal pol ORF annotated), and the paper's stated element length (9345 bp) matches the LOCUS length exactly. del is also the prototype of the Del/Tekay chromovirus lineage.

citation: Deposit: Hansen LJ, Sandmeyer SB (1990) J Virol 64(6):2599-2607, "Characterization of a transpositionally active Ty3 element and identification of the Ty3 integrase protein" (PMID 2159534). Label: Hansen LJ, Chalker DL, Sandmeyer SB (1988) Mol Cell Biol 8(12):5245-5256, "Ty3, a yeast retrotransposon associated with tRNA genes, has homology to animal retroviruses" (PMID 2854194) - "The inferred order of functional domains within TYB3--protease, reverse transcriptase, and endonuclease--resembles the order in Drosophila element 17.6 and in animal retroviruses but is different from that found in yeast elements Ty1 and Ty2."
why_safe: Ty3 is the type element that names the Ty3/Gypsy superfamily; the 1988 paper established, from domain order and RT similarity to Drosophila 17.6 (a gypsy-group element), that Ty3 is distinct from the Ty1/copia elements. That determination predates every TE annotation tool. This record is the transpositionally active Ty3 element: the feature table annotates the 5' sigma LTR (121..460) and 3' sigma LTR (5132..5471) with rpt_type=long_terminal_repeat, a complete gag3 CDS, and POL3; NCBI notes it "contains ICTV exemplar Saccharomyces cerevisiae Ty3 virus". The only non-element sequence is the flanking tRNA-Cys gene. (Note: the alternative Ty3-2 deposit M23367 was rejected because its feature table annotates no LTRs at all.)

citation: Poulter R, Butler M (1998) Gene 215(2):241-249, "A retrotransposon family from the pufferfish (fugu) Fugu rubripes" (PMID 9714821). Abstract: "Sequence comparisons of the predicted ORFs indicate that this element is related to the gypsy class of LTR-retrotransposons. Specifically, the sushi retrotransposons are most closely related to the retrotransposon group which includes the MAGGY retroelement ... and the CfT-1 element".
why_safe: The gypsy assignment is the discovery paper's own sequence comparison of the gag and pol ORFs against known gypsy-class elements, with a specific sister-group relationship to MAGGY/CfT-1 - not a pipeline call, and post-dating the Ty3/Gypsy vs Bel/Pao split so the "gypsy" term is used in its modern sense. The deposit is the element: mobile_element 1..5645 covering the whole record, with 5' LTR 1..560; the paper's stated full length (5.645 kb) matches the LOCUS length. Independent later corroboration exists in the sushi-ichi/SIRH-PEG10 domestication literature, and the record notes it contains the ICTV exemplar Takifugu rubripes Sushi virus.

organism: Trichoplusia ni (host); GenBank ORGANISM field is the ICTV virus taxon "Trichoplusia ni TED virus", host explicitly annotated /host="Trichoplusia ni"
citation: Friesen PD, Nissen MS (1990) Mol Cell Biol 10(6):3067-3077, "Gene organization and transcription of TED, a lepidopteran retrotransposon integrated within the baculovirus genome" (PMID 1692964). Abstract: "Determination of the complete nucleotide sequence (7,510 base pairs) of the integrated copy indicated that TED belongs to the family of retrotransposons that includes Drosophila melanogaster elements 17.6 and gypsy and thus represents the first nondipteran member of this invertebrate group".
why_safe: The primary paper assigns TED to the gypsy/17.6 group from pol-domain sequence similarity, and the assignment has been carried forward independently by ICTV, which places this record's source taxon in Metaviridae; Errantivirus; Errantivirus trichoplusiae - i.e. within Ty3/Gypsy. The paper's stated element length (7,510 bp) equals the LOCUS length exactly, and the record annotates the LTR (1..273), the tRNA primer binding site, and the three gag/pol/env-like ORFs, so the deposit is the element. Organism field note: the record's SOURCE organism is the ICTV virus taxon "Trichoplusia ni TED virus" with /host="Trichoplusia ni"; the biological host species (the moth in which TED is a retrotransposon) is Trichoplusia ni, which is what is reported here.

citation: Zhou Q, Haymer DS (1997) Genetica 101(3):167-178, "Molecular structure of yoyo, a gypsy-like retrotransposon from the mediterranean fruit fly, Ceratitis capitata" (PMID 9692226). Abstract: "This retrotransposon, which we named yoyo, appears to be a member of the gypsy/Ty3 class of elements ... The complete element is approximately 7.7 kb in size."
why_safe: The label is from the discovery paper (title and abstract both state gypsy/Ty3), published after the Ty3/Gypsy vs Bel/Pao distinction was recognised, and it is independently corroborated by ICTV, which uses this record as the exemplar for Ceratitis capitata Yoyo virus in the genus Errantivirus (Metaviridae, i.e. Ty3/Gypsy). The deposit is the element: mobile_element 1..7698 spans the whole record with 5' LTR 1..316, and 7,698 bp matches the paper's "approximately 7.7 kb". Confidence is medium rather than high because the primary claim is hedged ("appears to be a member") and rests on structural/similarity arguments rather than an explicit RT phylogeny; the corroboration is a taxonomic assignment rather than a published tree.

citation: Madsen LH, Fukai E, Radutoiu S, Yost CK, Sandal N, Schauser L, Stougaard J (2005) Plant J 44(3):372-381, "LORE1, an active low-copy-number TY3-gypsy retrotransposon family in the model legume Lotus japonicus" (PMID 16236148). The Ty3-gypsy family assignment is stated in the title and is the paper that describes and deposits LORE1a.
why_safe: The classification is the discovery paper's own, asserted in its title, and is reinforced independently by Fukai E et al. (2010) PLoS Genet 6(3):e1000868, "Derepression of the plant Chromovirus LORE1 induces germline transposition in regenerated plants", which treats LORE1 as a chromovirus - the chromodomain-bearing lineage inside Ty3/Gypsy. Neither statement derives from running an annotation tool on this record. The deposit is the element: repeat_region 137..5177 is annotated as "TY3-gypsy retrotransposon LORE1a" with its LTR (137..361) and a single 4527-bp ORF, inside a 5406-bp record. Adds an autonomous, transpositionally active eudicot (legume) element to the panel.

citation: Bae YA, Moon SY, Kong Y, Cho SY, Rhyu MG (2001) Mol Biol Evol 18(8):1474-1483, "CsRn1, a novel active retrotransposon in a parasitic trematode, Clonorchis sinensis, discloses a new phylogenetic clade of Ty3/gypsy-like LTR retrotransposons" (PMID 11470838). The Ty3/gypsy assignment, and the recognition of CsRn1 as a distinct clade within Ty3/gypsy, is the stated result of that paper.
why_safe: The label rests on an explicit molecular-phylogenetic analysis published in Mol Biol Evol - the paper's contribution is precisely the placement of CsRn1 within Ty3/gypsy - and is independent of any annotation software applied to this record. The deposit is the element: mobile_element 1..5008 spans the entire record, with the 5' LTR annotated at 1..471. This is the only lophotrochozoan/platyhelminth case in the panel, and one of the few Ty3/Gypsy elements with a published clade-level phylogeny outside plants, fungi and insects.

citation: Label: Nagaki K, Neumann P, Zhang D, Ouyang S, Buell CR, Cheng Z, Jiang J (2005) Mol Biol Evol 22(4):845-855 - "The centromeric retrotransposon (CR) family in the grass species is one of few Ty3-gypsy groups of retroelements that preferentially transpose into highly specialized chromosomal domains ... CRR (CR of rice) and CRM (CR of maize) elements"; further supported by Neumann P et al. (2011) Mob DNA 2:4 - "centromeric and pericentromeric regions of plant chromosomes are colonized by Ty3/gypsy retrotransposons, which, on the basis of their reverse transcriptase sequences, form the chromovirus CRM clade". Deposit: Zhong CX, Marshall JB, Topp C, Mroczek R, Kato A, Nagaki K, Birchler JA, Jiang J, Dawe RK (2002) Plant Cell 14(11):2825-2836 (PMID 12417704).
why_safe: Zhong et al. 2002 supplies the deposit (the CRM element used in the maize CENH3 ChIP study) but never states a superfamily; the Ty3-gypsy label is taken from two later phylogenetic studies that assign the CR/CRM family on reverse-transcriptase sequence, one of which (Neumann 2011) defines the CRM chromovirus clade from an RT tree over 190 elements. Neither is a per-record annotation call on AY129008. The deposit is the element: mobile_element 1..7572 covers the whole record, with a single 4857-bp gag-pol CDS. Gives the panel a bona fide CRM-clade chromovirus. Maize is already represented in the corpus by other families, but this accession is not.

citation: Nakayashiki H, Matsuo H, Chuma I, Ikeda K, Betsuyaku S, Kusaba M, Tosa Y, Mayama S (2001) Nucleic Acids Res 29(20):4106-4113, "Pyret, a Ty3/Gypsy retrotransposon in Magnaporthe grisea contains an extra domain between the nucleocapsid and protease domains" (PMID 11600699). The Ty3/Gypsy assignment is stated in the title of the paper that describes and deposits this element.
why_safe: The label is the discovery paper's own, based on its analysis of the polyprotein domain organisation, and predates the annotation tools under test. The deposit is the element: mobile_element 1..7250 spans the whole record. Pyret is a useful stress case because the paper's headline finding is a non-canonical extra domain inserted between the nucleocapsid and protease domains - a structure that domain-order heuristics can misread while the published superfamily label stays fixed. Note on overlap: the species (Magnaporthe/Pyricularia grisea) already appears in the existing corpus via MAGGY and grasshopper, but this accession and element family are distinct and not on the exclusion list.

citation: Haas NB, Grabowski JM, Sivitz AB, Burch JB. 1997. Chicken repeat 1 (CR1) elements, which define an ancient family of vertebrate non-LTR retrotransposons, contain two closely spaced open reading frames. Gene 197(1-2):305-309 (PMID 9332379). Supports: CR1 is a distinct, ancient vertebrate non-LTR retrotransposon family, and the full-length element carries two closely spaced ORFs.
why_safe: The label is in the title of the paper that deposited the record: the authors define CR1 as a vertebrate non-LTR retrotransposon family with two closely spaced ORFs. The record's own feature table encodes exactly that architecture with both ORFs intact and translated (ORF1 228..1490, ORF2 1493..4465, ending 93 bp before the record's end), so the autonomous full-length claim is attested by the deposit itself, not by any repeat-annotation pipeline. The deposit is a reconstructed consensus rather than one natural genomic locus - for a classifier benchmark that is an advantage (no locus-specific decay), but it should be recorded, and it means the case tests clade architecture, not a real insertion. Fills a genuine gap: the only CR1 currently in the corpus (D76434) is a 536 bp 5'-truncated fragment.

citation: Xiong Y, Eickbush TH. 1988. The site-specific ribosomal DNA insertion element R1Bm belongs to a class of non-long-terminal-repeat retrotransposons. Mol Cell Biol 8(1):114-123 (PMID 2447482). Supports: R1Bm is a non-LTR (non-long-terminal-repeat) retrotransposon that inserts site-specifically into 28S rDNA.
why_safe: The class assignment is the literal claim of the deposit paper's title - R1Bm 'belongs to a class of non-long-terminal-repeat retrotransposons' - and R1Bm is the type element after which the R1 clade is named. Independent of that, the record's feature table carries mobile_element 44..5135 with /mobile_element_type="retrotransposon:R1", flanked by an annotated 5' rDNA insertion target site (30..43), plus a gag CDS (519..1895) and a complete RT/ORF2 CDS (1885..5028): both ORFs are present and the element boundaries are annotated in the deposit, so nothing here depends on an annotation tool. Distinct from the corpus's R1Dm (X51968): different organism, different paper, and this is the original R1 element.

citation: Dombroski BA, Scott AF, Kazazian HH Jr. 1993. Two additional potential retrotransposons isolated from a human L1 subfamily that contains an active retrotransposable element. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 90(14):6513-6517 (PMID 8393568). Supports: L1.3 is one of 'the two remaining full-length members' of the L1 subfamily containing the active L1.2B element and 'contain[s] both open reading frames 1 and 2 intact'.
why_safe: Both the family label and the full-length/autonomous property come verbatim from the deposit paper's abstract: L1.3 is stated to be full-length and to have ORF1 and ORF2 intact, and to be a member of the same L1 subfamily as L1.2B, the element experimentally shown to have retrotransposed into the factor VIII gene. The 6059 bp record length matches the canonical ~6 kb full-length human L1. No feature annotation is present in the record and none is needed - the label rests on the paper. Caveat for panel balance, not accuracy: the corpus already contains three human L1 rows (AF148856 full-length, M22333 and M22334 truncated), so this adds a second independent full-length human L1 rather than a new taxon. It is retained because it is the cleanest primary-literature full-length statement available for the L1 clade.

citation: Deposit/structure: O'Hare K, Alley MR, Cullingford TE, Driver A, Sanderson MJ. 1991. DNA sequence of the Doc retroposon in the white-one mutant of Drosophila melanogaster and of secondary insertions in the phenotypically altered derivatives white-honey and white-eosin. Mol Gen Genet 225(1):17-24 (PMID 1705654) - supports that this record is the sequence of the Doc retroposon itself. Clade: Villasante A, Abad JP, Planello R, Mendez-Lago M, Celniker SE, de Pablos B. 2007. Drosophila telomeric retrotransposons derived from an ancestral element that was recruited to replace telomerase. Genome Res 17(12):1909-1918 (PMID 17989257) - states in its Discussion, in an RT-phylogeny paper on jockey-clade elements, that Dmel\Doc is among 'other members of the jockey clade such as, Dmel\Doc, Dmel\F, Dmel\Juan, and Dmel\X'.
why_safe: Despite the DEFINITION line naming the white locus, the whole deposit is the element: the feature table annotates mobile_element 1..4725 with /mobile_element_type="insertion sequence:Doc retroposon", so no coordinate extraction from a host locus is required. Both ORFs are complete, translated CDSs (ORF1 213..1910 RNA-binding protein; ORF2 1910..4576 reverse transcriptase), giving the canonical two-ORF jockey-clade architecture. The three misc_feature entries in the record were checked individually and mark secondary insertions found in OTHER derivative alleles (I factor in w-IR2, B104 in w-honey, pogo in w-eosin) - they are not disruptions of the white-one Doc copy deposited here, so the intact-autonomous framing holds. Confidence is medium rather than high solely because the Jockey-clade assignment rests on a passing (though peer-reviewed and phylogenetically grounded) Discussion statement in Villasante et al. 2007 rather than a dedicated clade table; the class-level non-LTR LINE call is high confidence from the deposit paper and record structure. Note the terminal misc_feature at 4693..4694 implies the element's 3' end is at or just before ~4692, i.e. the last ~30 bp may be flanking white sequence.

citation: Deposit: Schwarz-Sommer Z, Leclercq L, Gobel E, Saedler H. 1987. Cin4, an insert altering the structure of the A1 gene in Zea mays, exhibits properties of nonviral retrotransposons. EMBO J 6(13):3873-3880 (PMID 16453815) - states 'The longest Cin4 element analysed so far has two non-overlapping open reading frames (ORFs) comprising 2793 nucleotides (ORF1) and 3489 nucleotides (ORF2)', that ORF2 encodes a reverse-transcriptase-like protein, and that Cin4 elements end in an oligo(A) tract and are flanked by 3-16 bp target-site duplications. Clade: Smyshlyaev G, Voigt F, Blinov A, Barabas O, Novikova O. 2013. Acquisition of an Archaea-like ribonuclease H domain by plant L1 retrotransposons supports modular evolution. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 110(50):20140-20145 (PMID 24277848) - an RT-phylogeny analysis of plant L1 retrotransposons that names Cin4 as one of the plant L1-like families ('Cin4, the second plant L1-like retrotransposon family, was named after the Cin4 element from Z. mays').
why_safe: Class comes from the 1987 deposit paper's own title and abstract (nonviral/non-LTR retrotransposon with an RT-encoding ORF2, oligo(A) 3' terminus, flanking direct duplications). The L1-clade assignment comes from a later independent RT-phylogeny study of plant non-LTR elements, not from any annotation tool. The record's misc_features (orf1 1..2799, orf2 3088..6577) match the paper's stated 2793 nt and 3489 nt ORF sizes, so this deposit is the paper's longest/reference Cin4 copy rather than one of the heterogeneously 5'-truncated family members. Confidence is medium, not high, for two reasons stated honestly: (i) ORF1 begins at base 1 of the record, so there is no 5' UTR in the deposit and the element's true 5' terminus is unresolved - 'longest copy analysed' is weaker than 'complete'; and (ii) both ORFs are deposited as misc_feature, not CDS, so the record itself carries no translation attesting that the ORFs are uninterrupted.

citation: Deposit: Cambareri EB, Helber J, Kinsey JA. 1994. Tad1-1, an active LINE-like element of Neurospora crassa. Mol Gen Genet 242(6):658-665 (PMID 7512193) - the title itself asserts that Tad1-1 is an active LINE-like (non-LTR) element. Clade framework: Malik HS, Burke WD, Eickbush TH. 1999. The age and evolution of non-LTR retrotransposable elements. Mol Biol Evol 16(6):793-805 (PMID 10368957) - the RT-domain phylogeny that established the clade-level nomenclature for non-LTR retrotransposons; Tad1 is one of the recognised clades in this scheme and is eponymous with this element.
why_safe: The class label is the deposit paper's title claim ('an active LINE-like element'), and Tad is the experimentally demonstrated actively transposing element of Neurospora, so activity/autonomy is not inferred from sequence. Full-length status is attested structurally by the deposit itself: target-site duplications are annotated at BOTH ends as repeat_region order(36..50, 6974..6988), bracketing an ~6.9 kb element, with ORF1 (gag-like, CDS 158..1618) and ORF2 present - a complete element with both flanks, not a fragment. Confidence is medium rather than high only on the superfamily field: Tad1 is a legitimate non-LTR clade in the Malik/Burke/Eickbush RT-phylogeny scheme (and in Repbase's clade list), but it lies outside the six clades this panel enumerates, and I could not quote a sentence from Malik et al. 1999 naming Tad specifically because the clade roster is in the paper's figures, not the abstract. The class-level call is high confidence. Precedent for accepting a clade outside the enumerated set exists in the corpus, which already carries R4 (U29445) and I (M14954) under line-nonltr.

citation: Rosenzweig B, Liao LW, Hirsh D (1983) Sequence of the C. elegans transposable element Tc1. Nucleic Acids Res 11(12):4201-4209 (PMID 6306578) - deposit and original element description. Plasterk RHA, Izsvak Z, Ivics Z (1999) Resident aliens: the Tc1/mariner superfamily of transposable elements. Trends Genet 15(8):326-332 (PMID 10431195) - Tc1 named as the eponymous founding member of the superfamily.
why_safe: The Tc1/Mariner superfamily is named after this element, so the label is definitional and predates any annotation software. The deposit IS the element: mobile_element 1..1610 with mobile_element_type=transposon:Tc1 and inverted repeat_regions at 1..54 and 1557..1610. Record-level caveat: the flatfile annotates TWO CDS features, the 822-bp transposase (523..1344, UniProt P03934) and a shorter overlapping URF (605..943), so a classifier expecting a single clean transposase ORF will see two.

citation: Koga A, Suzuki M, Inagaki H, Bessho Y, Hori H (1996) Transposable element in fish. Nature 383(6595):30 (PMID 8779712) - discovery and deposit. Kawakami K, Shima A, Kawakami N (2000) Identification of a functional transposase of the Tol2 element, an Ac-like element from the Japanese medaka fish, and its transposition in the zebrafish germ lineage. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 97(21):11403-11408 (PMID 11027340) - the hAT ('Ac-like') assignment and the functional/autonomous transposase, both stated in the title.
why_safe: Family call comes from Kawakami et al. 2000, a primary paper whose title states 'an Ac-like element' (hAT) and which demonstrated transposition experimentally in the zebrafish germ line - independent of any annotation tool. The deposit IS the element (mobile_element 1..4682, terminal inverted repeats 1..19 and 4666..4682). Record-level caveat: the 1996-era feature table lists four separate unnamed CDSs (ORF1-ORF4) rather than the multi-exon spliced transposase later established by Kawakami; a caller expecting one transposase CDS will see fragmented ORFs.

citation: Mueller-Neumann M, Yoder JI, Starlinger P (1984) The DNA sequence of the transposable element Ac of Zea mays L. Mol Gen Genet 198(1):19-24 - deposit reference. Kunze R, Starlinger P (1989) The putative transposase of transposable element Ac from Zea mays L. EMBO J 8(11):3177-3185 (PMID 2555157) - the Ac transposase. Calvi BR, Hong TJ, Findley SD, Gelbart WM (1991) Evidence for a common evolutionary origin of inverted repeat transposons in Drosophila and plants: hobo, Activator, and Tam3. Cell 66(3):465-471 (PMID 1651170) - the paper that establishes the hAT grouping; Ac is the 'A' in hAT.
why_safe: Ac is the type element of the superfamily and the hAT grouping was established by protein-sequence comparison in Calvi et al. 1991, not by any pipeline. The deposit IS the element (mobile_element 1..4565, mobile_element_type=transposon:Ac element, imperfect inverted repeat annotated at 1..11). Record-level caveat: the feature table carries the original 1984-era ORF1/ORF2/ORF3 CDS calls, not the 5-exon spliced transposase defined by Kunze & Starlinger 1989, so the transposase is not present as a single contiguous CDS in this record.

citation: Pereira A, Cuypers H, Gierl A, Schwarz-Sommer Z, Saedler H (1986) Molecular analysis of the En/Spm transposable element system of Zea mays. EMBO J 5(5):835-841 (PMID 15957213) - full 8287 bp sequence of the autonomous En-1 element and its transcript structure.
why_safe: En/Spm is the type system of the CACTA superfamily and this is the autonomous (transposase-encoding) element itself, per the deposit title; record length 8287 bp matches the element length published by Pereira et al. 1986. Record-level caveat: this flatfile has NO mobile_element and NO repeat_region feature - the conserved CACTA terminal motif that names the superfamily is a property established in the primary literature, not something annotated in or verified from this deposit. The transposase is annotated as the multi-exon 'mosaic protein' (MP) gene with a 4.4 kb first intron, plus two internal ORFs, so it will not present as a single contiguous transposase CDS.

citation: Jiang N, Bao Z, Zhang X, Hirochika H, Eddy SR, McCouch SR, Wessler SR (2003) An active DNA transposon family in rice. Nature 421(6919):163-167 (PMID 12520302) - identification of Ping/Pong and the deposit itself. Zhang X, Jiang N, Feschotte C, Wessler SR (2004) PIF- and Pong-like transposable elements: distribution, evolution and relationship with Tourist-like miniature inverted-repeat transposable elements. Genetics 166(2):971-986 (PMID 15020481) - places PIF- and Pong/Ping-like elements in one superfamily (PIF/Harbinger).
why_safe: Family assignment comes from Wessler-lab comparative/phylogenetic analysis (Zhang et al. 2004), not from an annotation run. The deposit IS the element: mobile_element 1..5341, TIRs annotated at 1..14 and 5328..5341, ORF1 (2145..2663) plus a complete putative DDE transposase CDS (3190..4557) - the two-ORF architecture characteristic of PIF/Harbinger. Confidence held at medium for two reasons stated openly: (i) this is a Third Party Annotation record (KEYWORDS 'TPA:experimental', COMMENT states it uses data from DDBJ/EMBL/GenBank entry AP004236.1), and (ii) demonstrated autonomous transposition of Ping specifically is contested - much mPing mobilisation is attributed to the related Pong element - so the superfamily label is solid but the 'autonomous' claim should not be leaned on.

citation: Hershberger RJ, Warren CA, Walbot V (1991) Mutator activity in maize correlates with the presence and expression of the Mu transposable element Mu9. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 88(22):10198-10202 (PMID 1719548) - the deposit reference (element described there as Mu9). Chomet P, Lisch D, Hardeman KJ, Chandler VL, Freeling M (1991) Identification of a regulatory transposon that controls the Mutator transposable element system in maize. Genetics 129(1):261-270 (PMID 1657702) - independent identification of MuDR as the autonomous regulator of the Mutator system. Lisch D (2002) Mutator transposons. Trends Plant Sci 7(11):498-504 (PMID 12417150) - Mutator/MULE superfamily.
why_safe: MuDR is the autonomous type element of the Mutator-like element (MULE) superfamily, established genetically by two independent 1991 papers. The deposit IS the element: mobile_element 1..4942 with mobile_element_type=transposon:MuDR, ~215 bp inverted repeat_regions at 1..215 and 4728..4942, and both mudrA (transposase) and mudrB genes annotated as complete cds. The Mu9/MuDR naming equivalence is taken from the record's own qualifier /note='transposon formerly called Mu9', not from recollection.

citation: Kempken F, Kueck U (1996) restless, an active Ac-like transposon from the fungus Tolypocladium inflatum: structure, expression, and alternative RNA splicing. Mol Cell Biol 16(11):6563-6572 (PMID 8887685) - the paper title states the Ac-like (hAT) assignment and the element's activity.
why_safe: The hAT ('Ac-like') call is stated in the title of the primary description and rests on transposase sequence comparison to Ac/hobo/Tam3, not on any annotation pipeline. The deposit IS the element: mobile_element 1..4097 with mobile_element_type=transposon:restless, a 20 bp terminal inverted repeat at 1..20, and a spliced tnp transposase gene (CDS join(1460..1891,1939..3915)) with an experimentally mapped intron. The source feature also records /note='activity of transposon was shown experimentally'. Adds a fungal, non-plant non-animal data point for hAT.

citation: Langin T, Capy P, Daboussi MJ (1995) The transposable element impala, a fungal member of the Tc1-mariner superfamily. Mol Gen Genet 246(1):19-28 (PMID 7823909) - superfamily assignment stated verbatim in the title. Hua-Van A, Pamphile JA, Langin T, Daboussi MJ (2001) Transposition of autonomous and engineered impala transposons in Fusarium oxysporum and a related species. Mol Gen Genet 264(5):724-731 (PMID 11212928) - experimental demonstration of autonomous transposition.
why_safe: The Tc1-mariner assignment appears verbatim in the primary paper's title, derived from transposase (DDE) sequence comparison rather than from any annotation tool, and autonomy was demonstrated experimentally in 2001. The deposit IS the element and is exceptionally clean: mobile_element 1..1281 (mobile_element_type=transposon:impala), 27 bp inverted repeat_regions at 1..27 and 1255..1281, and one complete transposase CDS 133..1155 (AAB33090.2). Strain FOM24, clone imp160, subfamily E; organism recorded here at binomial rank, the deposit specifies forma specialis melonis. Note this record supersedes S75106.1.

expected_superfamily: Retroviridae, gammaretrovirus (MLV)-related clade; genus deliberately left unassigned by the describing authors (ZFERV)
citation: Shen CH, Steiner LA (2004) Genome structure and thymic expression of an endogenous retrovirus in zebrafish. J Virol 78(2):899-911. PMID 14694121. Abstract states verbatim: 'The provirus is 11.2 kb and contains intact open reading frames for the gag, pol, and env genes, as well as nearly identical flanking long terminal repeat sequences'; endogeneity from finding the provirus 'at the same genomic locus in sperm from four fish'; classification from 'Phylogenetic analysis indicates that it is closest to, yet distinct from, the cluster of murine leukemia virus-related retroviruses, suggesting that this virus represents a new group of retroviruses.'
why_safe: The ERV / LTR-retroelement call and the domain content are asserted in the primary describing paper's own abstract, not derived from any annotation pipeline; the record's feature table independently annotates 5' U3/R/U5 (1-513/514-626/627-695) and 3' U3/R/U5 (10555-11070/11071-11183/11184-11249), a gag-pro-pol polyprotein CDS (1890-8603, with programmed stop-codon suppression at 3960-3962) and an env CDS (8600-10531). The genus slot is deliberately hedged because Shen & Steiner explicitly decline to place ZFERV inside the Gammaretrovirus genus, calling it a new group; a benchmark that scores a bare 'Gammaretrovirus' answer as correct here would be scoring against the primary literature.

organism: Rhinella marina (host); ORGANISM field on the record is Rhinella marina endogenous retrovirus
citation: Russo AG, Eden JS, Enosi Tuipulotu D, Shi M, Selechnik D, Shine R, Rollins LA, Holmes EC, White PA (2018) Viral discovery in the invasive Australian cane toad (Rhinella marina) using metatranscriptomic and genomic approaches. J Virol 92(17):e00768-18. PMID 29899109. Abstract states verbatim: 'we also identified a complete genome sequence of a distinct epsilonretrovirus, Rhinella marina endogenous retrovirus (RMERV). The recently sequenced cane toad genome contains 8 complete RMERV proviruses as well as 21 additional truncated insertions. The oldest full-length RMERV provirus was estimated to have inserted 1.9 million years ago (MYA).'
why_safe: Genus assignment ('a distinct epsilonretrovirus') is stated in words by the authors who described the element, from their own phylogenetic analysis, and their endogeneity evidence is independent of any repeat annotator (8 complete proviruses plus 21 truncated insertions found in the assembled cane toad genome, with an insertion-age estimate). Record annotates both LTRs (1-471, 9739-10209) and gag (1207-3828), pol (3886-7680, 'protease, reverse transcriptase, integrase') and env (7668-9569) CDSs. Caveat for the benchmark: mol_type is RNA and the deposit is a Trinity assembly from a pooled liver transcriptome, i.e. a consensus provirus rather than a cloned genomic locus.

organism: Python molurus (host); ORGANISM field on the record is Python molurus endogenous retrovirus
expected_superfamily: Retroviridae, genus unassignable per the describing authors (PyERV) - NOT betaretrovirus, NOT gammaretrovirus
citation: Huder JB, Boni J, Hatt JM, Soldati G, Lutz H, Schupbach J (2002) Identification and characterization of two closely related unclassifiable endogenous retroviruses in pythons (Python molurus and Python curtus). J Virol 76(15):7607-7615. PMID 12097574. Abstract states verbatim: 'This virus contained intact open reading frames (ORFs) for gag, pro, pol, and env, as well as another ORF of unknown function within pol. Phylogenetic analysis showed that the virus is distantly related to viruses from both the B and D types and the mammalian C type but cannot be classified. It is present as a highly expressed endogenous retrovirus in all P. molurus individuals'.
why_safe: Both halves of the label come from the primary paper: the retroviral/ERV identity from ORF content plus presence in all individuals tested, and the explicit refusal to assign a genus from their own phylogeny. This makes it a deliberately hard case - the correct answer at genus level is 'unassigned', so any confident Betaretrovirus/Gammaretrovirus call should be scored wrong. Structural caveats for the benchmark: mol_type is RNA (cloned from sucrose-gradient-banded virion RNA, not from genomic DNA); the record has no LTRs at all (5'UTR <1..55, 3'UTR 7022..>7050 - coding core only); and the deposited Gag-Pro-Pol CDS carries an annotated 'artificial frameshift' join(177..1700,1700..2381,2381..5088). It therefore cannot test proviral boundary detection; env (5113-7032) and the internal domain order are what it tests.

organism: Gallus gallus (host); ORGANISM field on the record is Avian leukosis virus, independently classified by NCBI Taxonomy under Retroviridae; Orthoretrovirinae; Alpharetrovirus
expected_superfamily: Retroviridae, Alpharetrovirus (endogenous ALV subgroup E; chicken ev-3 locus)
citation: Johnson JA, Heneine W (2001) Characterization of endogenous avian leukosis viruses in chicken embryonic fibroblast substrates used in production of measles and mumps vaccines. J Virol 75(8):3605-3612. PMID 11264350. Abstract states verbatim: 'we examined the endogenous ALV proviruses (ev loci) present in a White Leghorn CEF substrate pool by restriction fragment length polymorphism. Five ev loci were detected, ev-1, ev-3, ev-6, ev-18, and ev-19. Both ev-18 and ev-19 can express infectious ALV-E, while ev-1, ev-3, and ev-6 are defective ... we defined the 1,692-bp deletion in the gag-pol region of ev-3'.
why_safe: The paper defines ev-3 as an endogenous (germline ev-locus) subgroup-E avian leukosis provirus and characterises its specific defect by sequencing, independent of any repeat annotator; the record itself carries /proviral, /strain='Endogenous avian leukosis virus 3; ev-3', /host='Gallus gallus', and annotates both LTRs (1-274, 5569-5842), the spliced env precursor Pr57 (join(554..571,3576..5402), gp85 + gp37) and a Pr112 gag-pol precursor (554-3688). Label chain stated openly: the paper's own term is 'endogenous ALV / ALV-E'; Alpharetrovirus is the ICTV genus of avian leukosis virus - the same kind of taxonomic-authority step the corpus already uses (e.g. the ICTV Metaviridae reference in the divergence-gradient rows). Deliberately hard case: because of the 1,692-bp gag-pol deletion the record is 5842 bp rather than ~7.5 kb, so a classifier requiring intact gag-pol will not find it, yet env and both LTRs are complete - the correct answer is still a defective ERV provirus carrying env.

expected_superfamily: Retroviridae, Betaretrovirus (type D; enJSRV lineage, clone enJS56A1)
citation: Palmarini M, Hallwirth C, York D, Murgia C, de Oliveira T, Spencer T, Fan H (2000) Molecular cloning and functional analysis of three type D endogenous retroviruses of sheep reveal a different cell tropism from that of the highly related exogenous jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus. J Virol 74(17):8065-8076. PMID 10933716. Abstract states verbatim: 'we molecularly cloned three intact type D endogenous retroviruses of sheep (enJS56A1, enJS5F16, and enJS59A1; collectively called enJRSVs)' and 'enJS56A1 had open reading frames for all structural genes, but it could not assemble viral particles when highly expressed in human 293T cells.'
why_safe: The 'type D endogenous retrovirus' call is in the paper's own title and abstract - type D is the classical morphological designation for the genus Betaretrovirus - and is supported there by the authors' own phylogenetic analysis distinguishing five ovine type D retroviruses. Clone-identity derivation, written down because the label attaches to the wrong element if it is wrong: the DEFINITION line never names enJS56A1, but the record's source qualifier reads clone='enJSRV 5.6A1', and the companion deposits from the same study are AF136224 clone='enJSRV 5f16' (6916 bp) and AF136225 clone='enJSRV 5.9A1' (6696 bp), so AF153615 is enJS56A1 by elimination and is the only one of the three deposited as a complete 7940 bp element. The feature table independently annotates both LTRs (1-447, 7496-7940) and Gag (583-2433), Pro (2325-3194), Pol (3440-5740), Env (5680-7515). Note: enJS56A1 has intact ORFs for all structural genes but is assembly-defective (Gag defect mapped by the authors to the first two-thirds of gag), so it is ORF-complete but not infectious. Distinct accession and distinct clone from the excluded DQ838493.

citation: Niebert M, Rogel-Gaillard C, Chardon P, Tonjes RR (2002) Characterization of chromosomally assigned replication-competent gamma porcine endogenous retroviruses derived from a large white pig and expression in human cells. J Virol 76(6):2714-2720. PMID 11861838. Title states 'gamma porcine endogenous retroviruses'; abstract states verbatim 'Two classes of polytropic type C porcine endogenous retroviruses (PERV) productively infect human cells in vitro' and 'we report the isolation of four full-length proviral sequences from a porcine bacterial artificial chromosome (BAC) library that comprises chromosomally assigned PERV. Clones Bac-PERV-A(130A12) and Bac-PERV-A(151B10) map to pig chromosome 1'.
why_safe: The gammaretrovirus / type-C assignment is stated by the authors in the paper title and abstract, and endogeneity plus chromosomal assignment (pig chromosome 1) come from their own BAC-library screen - no repeat-annotation tool is involved. Rule 4 is satisfied despite the BAC origin: the deposit itself is the 8911 bp full-length provirus, not the BAC clone, and its feature table annotates gag (1148-2725), pol (2873-6301, 'contains reverse transcriptase') and env (6177-8141), with ~1.1 kb and ~0.8 kb of unannotated flank at the two ends consistent with the LTRs. No claim is made here about replication competence of this particular clone: the retrieved abstract text is garbled at the point where it lists which clones were replication competent, so only the genus / type-C claim is relied on.

expected_class: not a TE - host telomerase reverse transcriptase catalytic subunit (TERT/p133)
citation: Collins K, Gandhi L (1998) The reverse transcriptase component of the Tetrahymena telomerase ribonucleoprotein complex. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 95(15):8485-8490. Claim supported: p133 is the catalytic reverse-transcriptase subunit of the Tetrahymena telomerase RNP, a single-copy host enzyme that maintains telomeres.
why_safe: Confusion axis: TERT carries an authentic RT fingers-palm-thumb fold with the canonical RT motifs, so any RT-HMM/domain-based TE caller can match it exactly as it matches LINE ORF2p or LTR pol. Tool-independence: Collins & Gandhi identified p133 by biochemical purification of the telomerase RNP and epitope-tagging/functional assay in Tetrahymena, not by homology search or repeat annotation. The deposit is the mRNA of a single-copy nuclear host gene, with no LTRs, no TIRs, no target-site duplications and no gag/transposase ORF.

expected_class: not a TE - host telomerase reverse transcriptase catalytic subunit (p123/TERT)
citation: Lingner J, Hughes TR, Shevchenko A, Mann M, Lundblad V, Cech TR (1997) Reverse transcriptase motifs in the catalytic subunit of telomerase. Science 276(5312):561-567. Claim supported: p123 is the catalytic subunit of Euplotes telomerase and contains bona fide reverse-transcriptase sequence motifs; the paper's entire point is that a host telomere-maintenance enzyme looks like an RT.
why_safe: Confusion axis: this is the landmark record establishing that a host enzyme carries RT motifs 1, 2 and A-E - the single most predictable false positive for an RT-domain TE classifier. Tool-independence: p123 was identified by biochemical purification of the Euplotes telomerase holoenzyme followed by mass-spectrometric peptide sequencing and reverse genetics in yeast (EST2), i.e. protein-level evidence entirely independent of any annotation pipeline. Discrete macronuclear gene deposit (CDS 101..3196), no terminal repeats, no TSDs, not multicopy. Uses ciliate genetic code (transl_table=10).

expected_class: not a TE - host AP (apurinic/apyrimidinic) endonuclease and strand transferase Rrp1, a single-copy DNA-repair gene
citation: Sander M, Lowenhaupt K, Lane WS, Rich A (1991) Cloning and characterization of Rrp1, the gene encoding Drosophila strand transferase: carboxy-terminal homology to DNA repair endo/exonucleases. Nucleic Acids Res 19(16):4523-4529 (sequence-of-record for this deposit; establishes the C-terminal homology to ExoIII/APE-family repair endo/exonucleases). Sander M, Lowenhaupt K, Rich A (1991) Drosophila Rrp1 protein: an apurinic endonuclease with homologous recombination activities. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 88(15):6780-6784, PMID 1713691 (establishes AP-endonuclease activity biochemically).
why_safe: Confusion axis: the Rrp1 C-terminal domain belongs to the Exo_endo_phos / DNase-I-like nuclease superfamily - the same fold as E. coli exonuclease III, human APE1 and the endonuclease (EN) domain of LINE-1 ORF2p - so an EN-domain-keyed TE caller is at genuine risk of flagging it. Tool-independence: AP-endonuclease and strand-transfer activities were measured on purified protein in vitro; the label rests on enzymology, not on similarity to a TE library. The record is an mRNA (complete cds) of a single-copy nuclear repair gene, so it cannot harbour an intronic element, and it carries no RT, no transposase and no terminal repeats. Complements the excluded human APEX1 row (NG_008718) with an invertebrate representative of the same fold.

expected_class: not a TE - host AP (apurinic) endonuclease / redox factor ARP, a base-excision-repair gene
citation: Murphy TM, Belmonte M, Shu S, Britt AB, Hatteroth J (2009) Requirement for abasic endonuclease gene homologues in Arabidopsis seed development. PLoS ONE 4(1):e4297. Claim supported: this is the record's own reference; it establishes genetically that the Arabidopsis abasic (AP) endonuclease genes, including ARP, are host DNA-repair genes required for normal seed development.
why_safe: Confusion axis: plant ARP is an APE1/ExoIII-family abasic endonuclease, i.e. the Exo_endo_phos/DNase-I-like fold shared with the LINE-1 ORF2p EN domain - the same trap as Rrp1, sampled from a second kingdom. Tool-independence: the cited paper's evidence is loss-of-function genetics (seed-development phenotype of insertion lines), not homology-based annotation. mRNA deposit, complete cds 9..1625, single locus, no LTR/TIR/TSD/RT/transposase content. Note: I deliberately did NOT cite Babiychuk et al. 1994 PNAS (the original Arabidopsis Arp AP-endonuclease enzymology) because I could not confirm that ACB29409.1 in this record is the same locus as Babiychuk's ARP - the two 'ARP' deposits encode proteins of different length (Z49776 CDS 49..1938 -> 629 aa vs this record's 538 aa) and Murphy et al. deposited multiple abasic-endonuclease homologues. The AP-endonuclease label is safe either way; only the choice of citation was affected.

expected_class: not a TE - phage-encoded tyrosine (lambda-integrase family) site-specific recombinase, Cre
citation: Sternberg N, Sauer B, Hoess R, Abremski K (1986) Bacteriophage P1 cre gene and its regulatory region. Evidence for multiple promoters and for regulation by DNA methylation. J Mol Biol 187(2):197-212 (sequence-of-record and gene identity). Argos P, Landy A, Abremski K, Egan JB, Haggard-Ljungquist E, Hoess RH, Kahn ML, Kalionis B, Narayana SV, Pierson LS 3rd (1986) The integrase family of site-specific recombinases: regional similarities and global diversity. EMBO J 5(2):433-440, PMID 3011407 (places Cre in the lambda-integrase/tyrosine-recombinase family).
why_safe: Confusion axis: Cre is a catalytic-tyrosine site-specific recombinase acting at loxP. The tyrosine-recombinase fold - not the DDE transposase fold - is exactly what Crypton DNA transposons and DIRS-like retroelements use for integration, so a recombinase/integrase-keyed classifier can plausibly call this an element. Tool-independence: Cre's recombinase function was established biochemically and genetically (in vitro loxP recombination with purified protein) decades before TE annotation tools existed, and the integrase-family assignment in Argos et al. is a manual comparative alignment of experimentally characterised recombinases. The deposit is a 1553 bp discrete gene record with no LTRs, no TIRs, no RT and no transposase; Cre acts on the phage genome in trans and is not itself a mobile unit. Complements the excluded E. coli XerC row (NC_000913.3) with a phage-origin recombinase, which the panel brief explicitly requested.

expected_class: not a TE - host ribonuclease HI (rnhA), a single-copy chromosomal RNase H gene
citation: Itaya M, Kondo K (1991) Molecular cloning of a ribonuclease H (RNase HI) gene from an extreme thermophile Thermus thermophilus HB8. Nucleic Acids Res 19(16):4443-4449 (sequence-of-record; functional complementation of an E. coli rnh mutant). Kanaya S, Itaya M (1992) Expression, purification, and characterization of a recombinant ribonuclease H from Thermus thermophilus HB8. J Biol Chem 267(14):10184-10192 (biochemical characterisation of the purified enzyme).
why_safe: Confusion axis: bacterial RNase HI is the reference fold for the RNase H domain carried in the pol polyprotein of every LTR retrotransposon/retrovirus and in many non-LTR elements, so an RNase-H-domain profile hit here is essentially guaranteed. Tool-independence: the label rests on in vivo complementation of an rnh-deficient E. coli strain and on Mg2+-dependent RNA:DNA-hybrid cleavage assayed with purified recombinant protein - enzymology, not annotation. The deposit is a 1062 bp discrete gene record for a single-copy housekeeping gene, with no RT, no integrase, no terminal repeats and no target-site duplications. Adds a thermophilic-bacterium taxon absent from the existing negative panel.

expected_class: not a TE - ordinary single-copy host protein-coding gene (ovalbumin, the archetypal serpin-family egg-white storage protein)
citation: McReynolds L, O'Malley BW, Nisbet AD, Fothergill JE, Givol D, Fields S, Robertson M, Brownlee GG (1978) Sequence of chicken ovalbumin mRNA. Nature 273(5665):723-728. Claim supported: the ovalbumin mRNA encodes the 385-residue chicken egg-white protein ovalbumin, an ordinary hormonally regulated host gene product.
why_safe: Confusion axis: none at the domain level - this is the easy-case control that should never be called. Its only risk is generic ORF/repeat heuristics. Tool-independence: ovalbumin was characterised by direct protein and mRNA sequencing in 1978 and by complete chromosomal gene sequencing (Woo et al. 1981 Biochemistry 20:6437-6446), long predating any TE caller. Identity of THIS deposit was checked by derivation rather than taken on trust: CDS 27..1187 = 1161 nt = 386 codons + stop = 385 aa, matching mature chicken ovalbumin exactly. I deliberately chose this mRNA deposit over the classic genomic record J00895 (9206 bp) because CR1 non-LTR elements are documented in the chicken ovalbumin gene domain, so a genomic deposit could legitimately contain a TE inside its introns and would be an unsafe negative; an mRNA cannot. Bird taxon is absent from the existing negative panel.

expected_class: not a TE - pericentromeric major satellite tandem repeat (234 bp monomer); satellite DNA, not a mobile element
citation: Horz W, Altenburger W (1981) Nucleotide sequence of mouse satellite DNA. Nucleic Acids Res 9(3):683-696. Claim supported: determination of the mouse satellite (major satellite) repeat unit sequence and its tandem, internally sub-repeated organisation.
why_safe: Confusion axis: highly abundant tandem repeat that trips repeat-content and low-complexity masking, which is the same signal many pipelines use to nominate TE candidates - but it has no ORF, no RT, no transposase, no LTRs and no TIRs, so it is a pure repeat-content false positive rather than a domain false positive. Tool-independence: satellite identity was established by buoyant-density fractionation and direct sequencing of the isolated satellite fraction, an experimental definition with no annotation step. The record length (234 bp) is the major-satellite monomer itself, so the deposit is the repeat unit, not a clone containing it. Complements the excluded human alpha-satellite row (X07685) with a rodent satellite of independent origin.
